facts: Historic centre of Jeddah, known for coral-stone houses with wooden roshan windows; inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014 (OSM whc:inscription_date=2014). The old city walls were torn down in the 1940s. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Balad,_Jeddah , https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1361
notes: Coordinates are the centroid of the OSM historic=district polygon (way/1192695373), not a single entrance. Website is the Wikidata-listed official Historic Jeddah programme site (returned an HTTP 509 bandwidth error when checked 2026-10-26); OSM also lists https://heritage.moc.gov.sa. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar / Wikidata ar label.

facts: Built between 1872 and 1881 for Omar Nasseef Effendi; King Abdulaziz (Ibn Saud) used it as a residence after entering Jeddah in 1925. It is now used as a cultural centre for exhibitions and lectures. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasseef_House
notes: OSM name:ar tag wrongly contains 'Naseef House'; Arabic name taken from Wikidata. Opening hours/fees not verified. Arabic name source: Wikidata ar label (OSM name:ar holds English text).

facts: Privately owned historic family house in Al-Balad run as a small museum of household antiques, near Souq Al-Alawi. Sources: https://www.lonelyplanet.com/saudi-arabia/jeddah/attractions/matbouli-house-museum/a/poi-sig/1611039 , OSM node/7156675185 (tourism=museum)
notes: No official website found. A ticket-reseller listing mentions ~10 SAR entry but this is unverified, so fee left null. Sources disagree on the building's age (Commons file titles say 1613; another listing says 19th century) - do not publish an age. No Arabic name in OSM/Wikidata.

image.commonsTitle: File:Al-Matbouli House, 1613, old Jeddah, Saudi Arabia (3) (50703576062).jpg
image.author: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

address: Khalid Bin Al Walid Street, Al-Balad, Jeddah 22236
facts: Gate on the eastern side of the old city, named for the road to Makkah; the city wall it belonged to was demolished in the 1940s and the gate is a reconstructed landmark. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Balad,_Jeddah , https://saudipedia.com/en/article/3090/history/landmarks-and-monuments/how-old-is-al-balad-district-in-jeddah
notes: Free-standing gate next to a busy road/souq area; no ticketing. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

image.commonsTitle: File:Bab Mecca, Old Jeddah, Saudi Arabia (1) (50703487276).jpg
image.author: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

facts: One of the historic gates of Jeddah's old city wall, on the northern edge of Al-Balad. Sources: https://saudipedia.com/en/article/3090/history/landmarks-and-monuments/how-old-is-al-balad-district-in-jeddah , OSM way/1106842821
notes: Sources differ on the gates' exact compass positions; keep copy generic. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: One of the historic gates of Jeddah's old city wall, at the southern edge of Al-Balad. Sources: https://saudipedia.com/en/article/3090/history/landmarks-and-monuments/how-old-is-al-balad-district-in-jeddah , OSM node/11640872514
notes: OSM has English name only ('Bab Sharif Gate'). No suitable Commons photo found.

facts: Historic mosque in the al-Mazloum quarter of Al-Balad, regarded as the oldest mosque in Jeddah and generally dated to the 13th century. It reopened in 2015 after a three-year restoration. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Shafi%27i_Mosque , https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/سوق_العلوي , https://reuters.screenocean.com/record/149082
notes: Active place of worship: visits outside prayer times, modest dress. OSM object is a tourism=attraction node named 'Al-Shafi’i' (no mosque polygon found via Nominatim). Arabic name source: Wikidata ar label (Q20424977).

facts: Historic mosque on Souq Al-Alawi; an inscription dates it to 1240 AH (c. 1824/25) and attributes it to the governor Mustafa Mimar Pasha. It is still used for prayer. Source: https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/مسجد_المعمار
notes: OSM start_date=1868 conflicts with the 1240 AH date on Arabic Wikipedia - do not publish a construction year until resolved. Active mosque. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: Historic multi-storey house with wooden roshan balconies on Al-Mathaf Lane in Al-Balad, mapped in OSM as a tourist attraction. Sources: OSM way/46613362, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Beit_Sharbatly.jpg
notes: Exterior is a landmark; whether the interior is open to visitors was not verified. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: Listed among the most famous and oldest historic houses of Al-Balad. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Balad,_Jeddah , OSM node/12525921301 ('House of the Baeshen Family')
notes: Interior access/opening hours not verified; OSM name:ar contains English text so Arabic name left null. No Commons photo found.

address: Bab Al-Bunt building, Historic Jeddah (Al-Balad), Jeddah
facts: Museum of the Red Sea's history and culture in the restored Bab al-Bunt building (originally built in 1866 as a sea gateway for pilgrims and travellers); it opened on 6 December 2025 with more than 1,000 objects in 23 galleries. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea_Museum , https://tradearabia.com/News/330755/Red-Sea-Museum-to-open-in-Historic-Jeddah-on-Dec-6/TTN
notes: Not found in OSM via Nominatim. Coordinates from Overture, cross-checked against geotagged CC0 Commons photos of the museum (21.4833-21.4835, 39.1832-39.1834). Official MoC subdomain (from Overture) did not respond from our network on 2026-10-26. Arabic name source: Wikidata ar label.

image.commonsTitle: File:Red Sea Museum Jeddah Saudi Arabia 004.jpg
image.author: Kolaiel

address: Culture Square, Jeddah Historic District, Jeddah
facts: The first teamLab Borderless digital-art museum in the Middle East, on the banks of Al-Arbaeen Lagoon at Culture Square in Historic Jeddah; it opened in June 2024. Sources: https://www.teamlab.art/e/jeddah/ , https://www.businesstraveller.com/business-travel/2024/06/03/teamlab-borderless-jeddah-to-open-on-june-10/
notes: Paid entry (OSM fee=yes; official site sells tickets and lists closure on Mondays, matching the OSM opening_hours). OSM address district is Al Baghdadiyah Al Gharbiyah; official address says Jeddah Historic District. No freely licensed photo found on Commons. Arabic name source: official site (teamlab.art/ar); OSM name:ar is misspelled 'تيم لاب بوليدرس جدة'. fee from OSM fee tag.

facts: Museum and cultural centre in Al-Balad dedicated to the Saudi composer and musician Tariq Abdulhakim; it was inaugurated by the Museums Commission in December 2023. Sources: https://saudipedia.com/en/tariq-abdulhakim-museum , https://visitsaudi.com/en/jeddah/attractions/tariq-abdulhakim-center-museum-albalad
notes: No standalone official website found (tickets via Ministry of Culture platforms). Arabic name not present in OSM/Wikidata.

address: Arwa bint Abdulmuttalib Street, Al Muhammadiyah, Jeddah
facts: Multidisciplinary arts complex run by Art Jameel, opened to the public in December 2021; it houses galleries, an independent cinema (Hayy Cinema), a library and studios. Sources: https://hayyjameel.org/ , https://arabnews.pk/node/1981291
notes: Not found in OSM; coordinates from Overture only (Nominatim reverse confirms the point is in Al Mohammadiyah, matching the official address). Official site (checked 2026-10-26) lists Wed-Mon 14:00-22:00, closed Tuesday - not stored in openingHours because it is not an OSM tag. Opened with free admission in 2021; current fee policy not verified. Arabic name source: official site (hayyjameel.org/ar).

nameEn: Al-Tayebat International City Museum (Abdul Raouf Khalil Museum)
address: Rayhanat al Jazirah Street, Al Faisaliyyah, Jeddah 23534
facts: Large private museum complex in Hejazi style founded by collector Abdul Raouf Khalil in Al-Faisaliyah; construction began in 1987 and it opened in 1996, with collections on Saudi heritage, Islamic civilisation and world cultures. Sources: https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/متحف_عبد_الرؤوف_خليل , https://saudipedia.com/ar/متحف-مدينة-الطيبات-العالمية-للعلوم-والمعرفة
notes: The 'Abdul Raouf Khalil Museum' and 'Al-Tayebat International City Museum' candidates are the same complex (merged). No official website found; a 2020 guide said it was closed for renovation, but press items from 2024 and 2026 describe it as active - confirm opening hours/fees before publishing. Overture also has a second 'Museum of Abdul Rauf Hasan Khalil' point at 21.5488,39.1682 that could not be verified (ignored). Arabic name source: Wikidata ar label (Q12238662).

image.commonsTitle: File:Tayebat City Museum, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia (2025).jpg
image.author: Saudi press Agency (SPA)

facts: Museum specialising in Islamic art, describing itself as the first of its kind in Saudi Arabia, with more than 1,000 pieces spanning 15 centuries (ceramics, metalwork, coins, manuscripts and Kaaba textiles). Source: https://www.iarts.sa/en/
notes: Not found in OSM. Wikidata and Overture coordinates agree (~100 m) and fall inside the Jeddah Park complex (OSM way/1316609645). Official site lists daily 10:00-22:00, Friday 17:00-23:00 (not stored as openingHours). Wikidata Arabic label is 'متحف دار الفنون الإسلامية'. Arabic name source: official site (iarts.sa).

address: شارع الملك خالد, An Nazlah Al Yamaniyah, Jeddah 21472
facts: Royal palace built 1928-1932 for King Abdulaziz in al-Nazlah al-Yamaniyah; it houses the Jeddah Regional Museum of Archaeology and Ethnography, opened in 1995. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khuzam_Palace , https://saudipedia.com/en/jeddah-regional-museum
notes: Could not confirm current public opening hours or whether the museum is open to walk-in visitors; no closure notice found either. Verify with the Heritage Commission before showing as open. Arabic name source: Wikidata ar label.

facts: Mosque built over the sea on the North Corniche, established in 1985; it covers 2,400 m2 and has one main dome and 52 smaller outer domes. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Rahmah_Mosque
notes: Active mosque; also known as Fatima Al-Zahra Mosque. Popularly called the 'floating mosque'. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

image.commonsTitle: File:Mezquita Al-Rahmah, Yeda, Arabia Saudita, 2025-05-19, DD 02.jpg
image.author: Diego Delso

address: al Corniche Road, Al Hamra, Jeddah 23212
facts: Offshore fountain built 1980-1983 whose jet reaches 312 m, listed by Guinness World Records as the tallest fountain in the world. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Fahd%27s_Fountain
notes: Coordinates are the jet itself, in the sea. It is viewed from the Al-Hamra (Middle) Corniche - see middle-corniche-park; Commons viewing photos are geotagged around 21.514-21.520, 39.152-39.154. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: A 171 m freestanding flagpole erected in 2014; it was the world's tallest flagpole until 2021. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeddah_Flagpole
notes: No OSM flagpole object found by name; Wikidata point lies on OSM 'King Abdullah Roundabout' (way/26935942). The base sits in a roundabout - it is a landmark to view rather than visit on foot. Arabic name source: Wikidata ar label.

facts: Redeveloped seafront promenade on the North Corniche, opened in 2017 and renamed ROSHN Waterfront under a 2022 sponsorship deal; it stretches about 4 km with recreation areas for families and children. Sources: https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/roshn-signs-agreement-to-sponsor-and-rename-jeddah-waterfront-805353566.html , https://www.wam.ae/en/article/b3ew7k3-jeddah-revamp-waterfront-walkway-that-attracts-55m
notes: Coordinates are the centroid of the OSM park polygon; the promenade is long, so consider showing it as an area. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: Public seafront park on the Al-Hamra (middle) section of the Jeddah Corniche, the stretch from which King Fahd's Fountain is usually viewed. Sources: OSM way/628514686, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeddah_Corniche
notes: OSM has English name only. Covers the public viewing area for King Fahd's Fountain requested in the brief.

facts: A 9 km tidal creek north of central Jeddah, a former river valley flooded by the Red Sea and a popular location for marinas and water sports. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obhur_Creek
notes: Coordinate is the OSM label node for the bay. Much of the shoreline is private resorts/chalets; a public promenade and beach (South Obhur Waterfront) is on the south shore around 21.724-21.728, 39.115-39.117 (from geotagged CC0 Commons photos, not OSM). Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: Lagoon on the western edge of Historic Jeddah whose banks hold Culture Square and teamLab Borderless Jeddah. Sources: https://www.businesstraveller.com/business-travel/2024/06/03/teamlab-borderless-jeddah-to-open-on-june-10/ , OSM way/1265765000
notes: OSM has English names only ('Lake Al-Arbaeen Park'; a separate node/11757704579 'Lake Arbaeen' is tagged wheelchair=yes). No Commons photo found.

facts: Large public park of about 130,000 m2 in central Jeddah opposite Al-Handasa Square, with a walking track, a cycle path and a big children's play area; Jeddah Municipality's project won a Landscape Middle East 2025 community-impact award. Sources: https://sabq.org/article/slH5Gym , https://www.alwatan.com.sa/ampArticle/1026029
notes: Opened during Jeddah Season 2022 and reopened after redevelopment in 2024 per Arabic press. Sources differ on walkway/green-area figures - avoid publishing exact lengths. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: Marina development on the North Corniche next to the Corniche Circuit, combining a private members' yacht club, a marina, the Marina Walk dining promenade and The Jeddah EDITION hotel. Source: https://jycmarina.sa/
notes: OSM fee=yes and website https://jeddahyc.com/ (now redirects to jycmarina.sa). The club itself is members-only; Marina Walk dining is the public-facing part. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar. fee from OSM fee tag.

facts: Amusement park on the Corniche in Ash-Shati, opened in 2004; its central building has an ice-skating rink, and rides include a Boomerang roller coaster, a Wild Mouse coaster and a log flume. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Shallal_Theme_Park
notes: Ride list per Wikipedia (stub, may be dated). No good freely licensed photo (only a 500 px coaster shot) - image omitted. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar (Wikidata: حديقة الشلال الترفيهية).

facts: Public aquarium on the Corniche next to Al-Shallal, with an underwater tunnel, a dolphin show, sea lions, penguins and sand sharks. Source: https://fakiehaquarium.com/
notes: Paid tickets sold on the official site (fee field left null because OSM has no fee tag). Arabic name source: official site (fakiehaquarium.com/ar).

facts: Indoor role-play 'city' for children inside Mall of Arabia; it opened in January 2015 as Saudi Arabia's first KidZania. Sources: https://www.attractionsmanagement.com/attractions-news/KidZania-launches-third-location-in-the-Middle-East/313603 , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mall_of_Arabia_(Jeddah)
notes: Not in OSM; Overture point (conf 0.99) lies inside Mall of Arabia. Official site is behind a bot check (HTTP 403) and no 2024-2026 news was found, so current operation is not independently confirmed.

address: King Saud Road, Al Manarat, Jeddah
facts: Outdoor water park in north Jeddah (Al Manarat / Al-Buhayrat) with online ticketing. Sources: https://cyanwaterpark.com , OSM way/1538979228 (check_date 2026-07-13)
notes: Official site markets itself as Saudi Arabia's first water park - unverified claim, not used. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

address: Al-Madinah Al-Munawwarah Road, King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah 23732
facts: Domed event venue on Madinah Road, opened in June 2021, 210 m in diameter and 46 m high; it was recorded as the world's largest continuous dome. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeddah_Super_Dome
notes: Events/exhibitions venue - only open during events. No free photo found. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

address: Prince Khalid Bin Abdullah Road, Jeddah 23733
facts: Sports complex about 30 km north of central Jeddah whose ~62,000-seat stadium, nicknamed 'The Shining Jewel', opened on 1 May 2014; it hosted 2023 FIFA Club World Cup matches. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Abdullah_Sports_City_Stadium
notes: Match/event-day access only. Commons candidates rejected: 'Jawhara Stadium.jpg' is copied from saudipics.com without a license review; 'Al-Jawhara2014.jpg' is under a Commons deletion request (Aug 2026). Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

nameAr: مدينة الأمير عبد الله الفيصل الرياضية
facts: Stadium built in 1970 in south-east Jeddah (Al-Waziriyah area), used by Al-Ittihad and Al-Ahli; capacity is about 27,000. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Abdullah_Al-Faisal_Sports_City_Stadium
notes: OSM object is the pitch (access=private) inside the stadium; match-day access only. The only Commons photo is credited to FIFA (taken from its X account) with a doubtful free license, so no image. Arabic name source: Wikidata ar label.

facts: 6.174 km street circuit with 27 turns on the Corniche beside the Red Sea; it hosted the first Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in December 2021 and the Formula E Jeddah ePrix since 2025. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeddah_Corniche_Circuit
notes: Coordinate is a point on one OSM raceway segment. Public access only during events; Wikipedia notes the F1 race schedule changed after 2025 - check the official site for current events. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: Multiplex in Red Sea Mall that opened in early 2019 with 12 screens, including an IMAX auditorium. Sources: https://motivatevalmorgan.com/2019/02/07/vox-cinemas-opens-at-red-sea-mall-in-jeddah/ , https://www.imax.com/md/theatre/vox-red-sea-mall-imax
notes: Screen count is from the 2019 opening. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar (brand name).

address: Prince Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Street, Al Aziziyah, Jeddah 21553
facts: 13-screen VOX multiplex in the Jeddah Park complex, opened in June 2024 with an IMAX with Laser screen and GOLD screens. Source: https://motivatevalmorgan.com/2024/06/10/vox-cinemas-opens-at-jeddah-park-in-saudi-arabia/
notes: Arabic name source: OSM name:ar (brand name).

facts: The first Muvi Cinemas location, inaugurated at Mall of Arabia in August 2019 with 15 screens including ScreenX. Sources: https://arabnews.pk/node/1538781 , https://www.argaam.com/en/article/articledetail/id/1308977
notes: OSM name has no Arabic tag.

facts: Nine-screen AMC cinema in Stars Avenue Mall, AMC's first in Jeddah (2021), with an IMAX with Laser auditorium. Sources: https://broadcastprome.com/news/amc-brings-nine-screen-luxury-cinema-to-jeddah , https://www.imax.com/md/theatre/amc-stars-avenue-9-imax
notes: Official AMC site returned HTTP 502 when checked; IMAX listing (updated 2026) still lists the venue.

facts: Escape-room venue in Al-Salamah. Sources: https://transitionescape.com/ , OSM node/12188777007 (leisure=escape_game)
notes: Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: One of the oldest markets of Historic Jeddah, running between Qabil Street and Souq Al-Badu; it is known for its attar, spice and perfume sellers, and Nasseef House and Matbouli House overlook it. Source: https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/سوق_العلوي
notes: Linear pedestrian street - coordinate is a point on the OSM way. The only Commons photo shows an unidentifiable side alley, so no image. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: Historic market street in Al-Balad established in the early 1900s and named after merchant Suliman Qabil, who bought it in 1925-26; shops sell spices, household goods, perfumes and jewellery. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Souq_Qabil
notes: Linear pedestrian street - coordinate is a point on the OSM way. Arabic name source: Wikidata ar label / OSM alt_name.

facts: Shopping mall on King Abdulaziz Road in Al-Shatee, opened in 2008; it houses the VOX Cinemas multiplex. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea_Mall , https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q7305003
notes: Arabic name source: Wikidata ar label.

facts: Shopping mall in Al-Nuzha opened in October 2008; it contains KidZania Jeddah and the first Muvi Cinemas. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mall_of_Arabia_(Jeddah) , https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q6743988
notes: Official website (from OSM/Wikidata) did not respond from our network on 2026-10-26. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

address: Prince Majid Road, Al Faiha'a, Jeddah 22245
facts: Shopping mall on Prince Majid Road in Al-Faiha'a. Source: OSM way/194983990
notes: OSM opening_hours is '24/7', which is implausible for a mall, so openingHours left null. No official website confirmed. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

facts: Shopping mall in Al-Shatee on Al Salam Street. Source: OSM way/111645503
notes: OSM has English name only; no official website confirmed.

facts: Shopping mall in Al-Zahra that houses AMC Cinemas' nine-screen Jeddah cinema. Sources: OSM way/53202643, https://www.imax.com/md/theatre/amc-stars-avenue-9-imax
notes: No official website confirmed; no free photo found. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

address: Al Sayyedah Khadejah St., Al Faisaliyyah, Jeddah 21553
facts: Four-level shopping mall in Al-Faisaliyah opened on 18 May 2005. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serafi_Mega_Mall , https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q7452608
notes: OSM lists a mobile phone number; no official website found. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

address: Al Suaways St., Al Faisaliyyah, Jeddah 23451
facts: Shopping mall in Al-Faisaliyah. Source: OSM way/961659291
notes: No official website confirmed. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

address: Prince Majid Road, Al Faiha'a, Jeddah 22244
facts: Shopping mall on Prince Majid Road in Al-Faiha'a, near Al-Andalus Mall. Source: OSM way/219243591
notes: OSM opening_hours is '24/7' (implausible), so openingHours left null. No official website confirmed. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

address: Al Ajwad st. شارع الاجواد, Al Manar, Jeddah 23452
facts: Shopping mall in Al-Manar operated by Cenomi Centers. Sources: https://centers.cenomi.com/sa-en/malls/yasmeen/ , OSM way/961659639
notes: Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

address: Al Harameen Road, King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah 23743
facts: Shopping centre on Al Harameen Road in north Jeddah. Sources: OSM way/1135805160 (shop=mall), https://thevillage.sa/
notes: Website (from Overture) is behind a bot check (HTTP 403) - domain exists but content not read. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar.

address: King Fahd Road, Al Aziziyah, Jeddah 23334
facts: Retail and entertainment complex on King Fahd Road in Al-Aziziyah that houses a 13-screen VOX cinema (opened 2024). Sources: OSM way/1316609645, https://motivatevalmorgan.com/2024/06/10/vox-cinemas-opens-at-jeddah-park-in-saudi-arabia/
notes: OSM website tag points to visitsaudi.com (not official); the Cenomi operator page could not be read (bot check), so website null. Not a public green park despite the name.

nameEn: Tahlia Street (Prince Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Street)
address: Prince Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Street, Al-Rawdah, Jeddah 23326
facts: Fashion and shopping street in mid-town Jeddah lined with designer boutiques and upscale department stores. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tahliah_Street_(Jeddah)
notes: Point is the Wikidata coordinate on the central commercial stretch (lies on OSM way/38500585); the street runs ~10 km, so treat as an area. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar / Wikidata ar label.

image.commonsTitle: File:Prince Mohammed Bin Abdulaziz St. near Le Mall, Tahlia, Jeddah.jpg
image.author: Lightdn

address: Al-Madinah Al-Munawwarah Road, Ash Sharafiyah, Jeddah 22234
facts: Mosque in Al-Sharafiyah designed by architect Abdel-Wahed El-Wakil and completed in 1987; its main dome is 42 m high and the minaret 60 m. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Saud_Mosque
notes: Active mosque - visits outside prayer times, modest dress. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar / Wikidata ar label.

address: Qadat Al Fekr Street, Ar Ruwais, Jeddah 23218
facts: Nine-screen Muvi cinema in Ar-Ruwais (OSM screen=9, last surveyed 2026-07-24). Sources: OSM node/14046790501, https://www.muvicinemas.com
notes: Appears to be inside or next to Haifaa Mall (OSM way/334688043, ~170 m away) but the host mall was not confirmed; Haifaa Mall itself was left out because its operator page gives a conflicting street address. Arabic name source: OSM name:ar (brand name).
